name: Daher TBM 700–960
summary: Fast single-engine pressurized turboprop built in France, popular with US owner-pilots.

wings: Low, tapered wing; winglets on the TBM 900 and later
engines: Single PT6A turboprop in a long nose; four-blade prop on early models, five-blade on the 900 series and later
fuselage: Compact, stout fuselage with a few rectangular windows
Main door at left rear; many also have a separate pilot door at front left
tail: Swept fin with a long dorsal fillet

tellTales: Single turboprop with a conventional low tail and a stout fuselage
Winglets and a five-blade propeller on later models
Short, tapered wing with wide-track main gear

confusedWith.howToTell: The TBM is a larger, stouter aircraft with a shorter tapered wing, wide-track gear and (on the 900 and later) winglets; the PA-46 has a slimmer fuselage and a long, slender wing without winglets.
The TBM has a conventional low tail; the PC-12 is larger with a T-tail.
The TBM has a turboprop with exhaust stacks and retractable gear; the Cirrus SR has a piston engine and fixed gear.
The Epic has larger oval windows, a longer tapered nose and no winglets; the TBM has smaller rectangular windows and a shorter nose (900-series has winglets).
